question: Partly shared. Both papers address progression from MCI to AD in ADNI-MERGE MCI participants (progressive against stable MCI), so the task, comparison and population class match. As recorded, however, the pair sets P-334's florbetaben amyloid-PET univariate AUC (0.84) against P-168's LSTM on neuropsychological tests, FreeSurfer MRI volumes and demographics (0.93). P-168 uses no PET, so the channel being compared is not shared, and condition 1 fails for the pair as recorded. P-334 also prints single-feature AUCs on the channels P-168 does use (ADAS13 0.83, mPACCtrailsB 0.83, hippocampus 0.75), so a shared-channel comparison exists; it is judged under conditions 3 and 4. Differences allowed under condition 1: P-334 fits no model and labels visit records (pMCI records only within 3 years before conversion), while P-168 predicts participant-level conversion within 2 years of a 24-month index exam from five visits.
metric: ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC (match). P-334's values are univariate, record-level descriptive AUCs from no fitted model and no validation. P-168's are 10-fold cross-validated AUCs of multivariable models.

figures.P-334: Univariate AUCs, no interval printed: FBB 0.84, ADAS13 0.83, mPACCtrailsB 0.83, hippocampus 0.75. Hanley-McNeil at the participant counts (348 pMCI / 487 sMCI), which gives the narrowest possible interval because records, not participants, are the unit and within-person clustering is ignored. FBB 0.84: Q1 = 0.84/1.16 = 0.7241, Q2 = 2(0.84^2)/1.84 = 0.7670, SE^2 = [0.84*0.16 + 347*(0.7241-0.7056) + 486*(0.7670-0.7056)]/169476, SE = 0.0147, CI [0.811, 0.869]. ADAS13 0.83: SE = 0.0150, CI [0.801, 0.860]. Hippocampus 0.75: SE = 0.0176, CI [0.716, 0.784].
figures.P-168: 347 MCI participants at the 24-month index exam, 77 converters / 270 non-converters. LSTM with five visits of NP tests + MRI + demographics: AUC 0.93 +/- 0.06 (fold spread). Hanley-McNeil at 77/270: Q1 = 0.8692, Q2 = 0.8963, SE = 0.0206, CI [0.890, 0.970]. Single-time-point random forest (all modalities at 24 months): 0.90 +/- 0.09, CI [0.853, 0.947]. NP-only LSTM 0.89, CI [0.841, 0.940]. MRI-only LSTM 0.86, CI [0.805, 0.915]. Single-feature discrimination derived from Table 1 group means and SDs at the index exam (binormal, AUC = Phi(|m1-m0|/sqrt(s1^2+s0^2))): ADAS-cog 13, 21.74 +/- 7.09 against 12.90 +/- 5.73, gives Phi(8.84/9.116) = Phi(0.970) = 0.834. Hippocampal volume, 0.39 +/- 0.07 against 0.47 +/- 0.09, gives Phi(0.702) = 0.759. mPACC-trailsB, -8.83 +/- 3.62 against -3.13 +/- 3.81, gives Phi(1.085) = 0.861.

matched_figure_check: A matched single-feature comparison can be made from P-168's printed data, and it reconciles the pair on the shared channel. P-334 reports only single-feature AUCs and P-168 only multivariable models. P-168's Table 1 gives the index-exam distributions of the same single features, and their binormal AUCs agree with P-334's: ADAS13 0.834 against 0.83 (P-334's interval [0.801, 0.860]); hippocampus 0.759 against 0.75 ([0.716, 0.784]); mPACCtrailsB 0.861 against 0.83. At the level P-334 measures, the two papers' data therefore agree. The remaining gap (0.83 against 0.89-0.93) sets one feature against 15 tests, 7 volumes and five visits. P-168's own figures show that step: MRI-only 0.86 and NP-only 0.89 are both above its single-feature values, and the single-time-point model gives 0.90 against 0.93 for the longitudinal one. The derivation assumes approximately normal distributions within groups, since P-168 prints no per-feature AUC.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply. No compared AUC reaches 0.97 (the maximum is 0.93). P-334 fits no model, so near-ceiling overfitting does not arise. P-168 uses 10-fold CV on 347 participants with no external cohort.
reason: As recorded, the pair compares an amyloid-PET univariate AUC (P-334) with a model on cognitive tests and MRI that contains no PET (P-168), so the channel is not shared (condition 1). On the shared cognitive and MRI channels, P-168's printed group statistics give single-feature AUCs (ADAS13 0.834, hippocampus 0.759) that match P-334's (0.83, 0.75) within P-334's intervals. The headline gap is therefore one marker against a multi-feature longitudinal model (15 NP tests, 7 MRI measures and 3 demographic variables over five visits), which P-168's own data resolve (condition 3).

quotes.quote: Our findings showed the strong predictive potential of PET, particularly florbetaben (FBB), which achieved an AUC of 0.84.
categorizing 487 individuals as sMCI and 348 as pMCI.
Only records preceding the AD diagnosis and those within the 3-year window before the conversion event receive labels.
The AUC spans from 0.54 to 0.75 in MRI features, with the hippocampus exhibiting the highest AUC value.
In neurocognitive tests, the ADAS group demonstrates robust predictive power (AUC range from 0.80 to 0.83).
The longitudinal LSTM model showed superior prediction performance of MCI-to-AD progression (AUC 0.93 ± 0.06) compared to the random forest model (AUC 0.90 ± 0.09).
The study included 347 participants with MCI at 24-month (age: mean 75, SD 7 years; 39.8% women) from ADNI, of whom 77 converted to AD over a 2-year follow-up period.
The LSTM model utilizing longitudinal data reached the best performance, comparing to an AUC of 0.86 when using MRI measures.
In terms of NP tests, the LSTM model outperformed the random forest model, achieving an AUC of 0.89 compared to 0.87.
